chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He disliked wearing the shirt hemmed with brocade, and disliked wearing silk, and wearing embroidered qassi (fine linen/cotton), and disliked wearing the red cushion cover (mitharah), for it is the cushion of Iblis.
ai.seo_question: What types of clothing and fabrics did Imam al-Sadiq dislike wearing?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) extends the prohibition of luxury to specific garments and accessories, identifying the red 'mithara' (a type of cushion or cover) as the 'cushion of Iblis' to symbolize pride and extravagance. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between permissible adornment and the ostentatious display of wealth that leads to spiritual arrogance, a theme deeply rooted in the concept of 'zuhd' (asceticism) within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition.
